notes:
I wasn't able to write any notes on Psalm 25 this time, because I couldn't get any source pages to load.

**What happened:** I tried to load eight pages at once: Enduring Word, Precept Austin, BibleHub's Gill, Ellicott and Pulpit Commentary, Augustine's psalm commentary on New Advent, the NET Bible notes, and Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* on Blue Letter Bible. That went over the tool's usage limit, so nothing came back. I then tried Enduring Word on its own, but I had already used up my tool calls for this turn. No page text reached me.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, with a URL for every point, and not to fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written any verse notes.

**What I can do next:** In a new turn I'll fetch the pages one or two at a time, in this order:

1. **Main verse-by-verse sources:** Enduring Word, then BibleHub's Gill, Ellicott and Pulpit Commentary, then Precept Austin and Spurgeon's *Treasury of David*.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** pages on Desiring God, Ligonier, Wesley Center, Seedbed and LCMS/1517 about the verses most likely to be debated. These are v. 7 and v. 11 (forgiveness and "for Your name's sake"), v. 14 (the Lord confiding in those who fear Him) and v. 21 (integrity preserving me).
3. **Other views:** the NET Bible notes (for example, that the psalm is an acrostic, each verse starting with the next Hebrew letter), Augustine on New Advent (his numbering is Psalm 24), and any page discussing v. 13's "dwell in prosperity" alongside prosperity teaching.

Reply "continue" and I'll start, giving each note with its URL as I go.
